question.text: The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate $\lim_\limits{x \to \,\,-2} f(x).$
question.explanation:
As $x$ approaches $-2$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ grows to infinity, and therefore

\[ \lim_\limits{x\to -2^+} f(x)=\infty. \]

However, as $x$ approaches $-2$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty$, and therefore

\[ \lim_\limits{x\to -2^-} f(x)=-\infty. \] Consequently, \[ \lim_\limits{x\to -2} f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

question.text: The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate $\lim_\limits{x \to \,5} f(x).$
question.explanation:
As $x$ approaches $5$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty$, and therefore

\[ \lim_\limits{x\to 5^-} f(x)=-\infty. \]

However, the function is not defined for $x \gt 5,$ and consequently, we cannot approach $x=5$ from the right. So we have \[ \lim_\limits{x\to 5^+} f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

Therefore, \[ \lim_\limits{x\to 5} f(x)=\text{DNE}. \]

question.text: The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate $\lim_\limits{x \to \,-1} f(x).$
question.explanation:
We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $-\infty.$ So, the left-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow (-1)^-} f(x) = -\infty \, . \]

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $-\infty.$ So, the right-hand limit is

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow (-1)^+} f(x) = -\infty \, . \]

Consequently,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow -1} f(x)=-\infty \, . \]
